title: The Note Under the Ice

plate.narration: A fold in the air shivers at the end of the passage. Salt wind slips through, though the glacier lies all around. A low note trembles under the rock. Something here is waiting for an answer.

goal.text: Search the glacier for another opening.

steps.label: Follow the herd's ears to the ridge
Find what is making the ticking
Decide what to do about it

search.narration: You stay at the singing hall instead of taking the shelf path. Your job today is to search the glacier for another opening. The seam you tested stays sealed. The yeti herder waits at the door with the kid goat under one arm. "My herd keeps stopping at the east ridge," she says. "Ears up, all one way. Something up there ticks. Find it before a goat does."

variants.text: The passage behind the singing hall is as you left it, and the fold is still awake. Out in the snow, the herder waves with the kid goat under one arm. Walk back to the fold, or search the glacier again with her?

back_at_fold.narration: You walk back down the passage. The herder's cairn still guards its mouth. The fold waits, wide and steady, with salt wind on your cheeks.

plan.narration: The herder points at the east ridge. "Soft snow up there. Haul the sled, or go light?" Her sled has a coil of rope and a lantern tied on. The kid is chewing the rope. By the door, the hay pile is shorter than yesterday.

plan_a.narration: You load the rope, the lantern and a bundle of hay. The kid climbs on the hay and will not get off. "Every hand on the rope," says the herder. "Hay is heavy when it has opinions."

plan_b.narration: You tie the lantern to your belt and loop the rope across your chest. The kid trots ahead. "Keep moving," says the herder. "The crust only holds you if you do not stop."

climb_a.prompt: Every hand on the rope! Haul the sled up the soft slope.

climb_b.prompt: Scramble up the crust. Light feet, no stopping!

climb_done.narration: At the top, the wind goes quiet. A line of goats stands on the ridge, ears pointed west, toward the hall. The kid joins them and points its ears too, very seriously.

climb_slip.narration: The crust cracks, and you slide back. The kid bleats with laughter. The herder hauls you up by the rope. On the ridge, a line of goats points their ears west, toward the hall.

ridge.narration: The ridge is bare ice and wind. A dark hole the size of a bucket breathes out a cold, hooting draft. "A goat once fell asleep in there," says the herder. "He still brags about it." Tick. Tick. Tick. Something ticks, very faintly. Is the hole the answer?

ridge_a.prompt: Lie flat, ear to the ice, and follow the ticking to its loudest spot.

ridge_b.prompt: Test every draft with a wet finger. Quick, the wind keeps changing!

ridge_chime.narration: You ring the chime over the hole. One clear note, not sour, no echo. Away from a rift, Orin said, it is only a very small bell. The hole is just wind in a tube of ice.

ridge_done.narration: The hole only hoots. The real ticking is west, toward the hall, and low, under the ice. You pack snow around the hole so no goat noses in. "One less worry," says the herder.

ridge_off.narration: The wind swings, and the hole hoots at you rudely. You lose the trail. Then the kid sits down right where the ticking is loudest: west, and low. You pack snow around the hole so no goat noses in.

holes.narration: West of the hole, three snow mounds lie in a row, and the ticking jumps between them. The kid dives into one and pops out of another. "Watch the tail," says the herder. "Where does it end up?"

interaction.cue: Watch the kid dive between the mounds, then pick where it ends up.

onSuccess.narration: Right mound! The kid has its ear pressed to ticking ice. It sneezes on your boots.

onFailure.narration: Empty! The kid pops out next door and sits on the ticking ice to help.

onAssisted.narration: The herder holds the kid still, right by the ticking ice.

kid.narration: A gust shoves the kid sideways. It slides on its belly toward thin ice over a melt pool. The herder is too heavy to follow. "Kid!" she calls. The kid is having the best day of its life. How will you stop it?

kid_a.prompt: Throw the rope loop over the kid's horns!

kid_b.prompt: Sing the low hall note so the kid turns toward you.

kid_wing.narration: A winged friend leaps into the wind and glides over the thin ice. Everyone else keeps the rope ready for the catch.

kid_wing_check.prompt: Glide low and grab the kid, with the rope ready behind you.

kid_done.narration: The kid pops into your arms and licks your chin with a very cold tongue. "Good kid," says the herder. "Terrible kid. Same kid." She tucks her lunch bundle into your pack. "For the climb. Do not tell the kid."

kid_off.narration: You miss. The kid slides into a soft drift and pops out with a snowy beard, very pleased. The herder tucks it in her coat, where it chews her buttons.

crack.narration: West of the ridge, the glacier splits in a long crack. Steam curls out, smelling like warm wet wool. The ticking comes from below. A narrow snow bridge crosses it. "My herd goes the long way around," says the herder. "Safe, but slow."

crack_a.prompt: Rope up! Step across the snow bridge, light and quick.

crack_b.prompt: Read the cracks and shadows. Find the safest curve around.

crack_wing.narration: A winged friend flies the rope over the steam and ties it to a rock. The others cross the snow bridge with a hand on the line.

crack_wing_check.prompt: Fly the rope across the steam and tie it fast.

crack_done.narration: On the far side, the herder counts heads. The right number is her favorite sum. Steam fogs everyone's eyebrows. The ticking is almost under your boots now.

crack_slip.narration: The snow gives way. You slide onto a warm, steamy ledge below. The herder hauls you up, grunting. Your pride hurts more than your knee. The ticking is almost under your boots now.

post.narration: Under a lip of ice stands an old yeti listening post: a pole topped with a carved ice cup, like a giant ear. "My grandmother's," says the herder. "She never found out what ticked. Put an ear in and tell me." Here the ticking is louder, and it has a beat.

post_a.narration: You hum the low hall note into the cup. The ice hums back, a little flat. The ticking answers a beat later. The herder's ears go up. "It is listening. Do not stop."

post_b.narration: You count against your heartbeat. Tick, tick, pause, tick. It repeats. The kid counts too, with its hoof, wrongly and very confidently.

post_a_check.narration: The herder joins your note, then goes quiet to hear what answers.

post_b_check.narration: You draw the ticks in the snow. The herder sets a claw beside each mark. Her grandmother listened here too.

post_done.narration: The pattern matches the song you learned in the hall: slow, slow, quick. The ticking is the hall note, answered from far below. "Under the hall," says the herder. "Of course."

warm.narration: The herder sets out a little stove of warm stones. The kid falls asleep on someone's boots. "Find where the ticking goes, and maybe I find a way to feed my herd," she says. "The tunnel below is too narrow for me. I will go around by the hall's back door and meet you." She gives you a jar of glowing moss. "Mosslight. For dark places."

tunnel.narration: The tunnel mouth is a low arch of clear ice. Beyond it is dark. Your footsteps come back to you late, like a shy echo. The ticking goes on ahead. How will you find your way?

tunnel_a.narration: You run the lantern along the wall, a stretch at a time. Frost makes patterns, mostly feathers. One stretch looks like a row of little stitches.

tunnel_b.narration: Hand on the shoulder in front, eyes closed, you hum the hall note. It comes back from the left, then from lower down. The ice hums like a very large, very shy cat.

tunnel_star.narration: A starweaver breathes on the wall, and the frost sparkles. The ticking line shows up like a path of tiny stars. The others hold the lantern steady.

tunnel_moss.narration: You open the herder's jar. Soft light spills out, and the ticking line shines on the wall like tiny stitches. The moss fades as you go, and you tuck the empty jar away.

tunnel_moss_check.prompt: Follow the shining stitches along the wall.

tunnel_a_check.prompt: Study the wall, stretch by stretch, and spot the line of ticks.

tunnel_b_check.prompt: Hum together and follow the loudest echo, hand on shoulder.

tunnel_star_check.prompt: Read the starlit frost and lead the way.

tunnel_done.narration: The ticks run along the wall like stitches, then turn down to a crack at the tunnel's end. There, the tunnel shrinks around you. You will have to squeeze.

tunnel_off.narration: The frost blurs into feathers and more feathers. You bump the same wall twice. The third time, you feel ticks under your hand. They lead to a crack where the tunnel shrinks around you.

squeeze.narration: The crack fits one body at a time, and no packs. Through it, the ticking is louder. Cold air slides out, smelling faintly of salt. Part of the roof looks loose. How will you get through?

squeeze_a.prompt: Chip the crack wider with the rope hooks.

squeeze_b.prompt: Smallest first, packs on the rope, nobody stuck. Work out the order.

squeeze_brace.narration: A thornguard plants both feet and holds up the loose roof. The others edge past, one at a time, with the packs on the rope.

squeeze_slip.narration: A duskrunner slides through like a ribbon and ties the rope to a knob of ice. The packs go over the rope, and the others follow.

squeeze_brace_check.prompt: Hold the roof up while everyone edges through.

squeeze_slip_check.prompt: Slip through and tie the rope on the far side.

squeeze_done.narration: The crack is wide enough now. As you edge in, ice chips pat down from the roof. It gives a long, low creak.

squeeze_off.narration: The crack is only half as wide as you hoped. Ice chips rain on your heads, and the roof creaks. Everyone gets frosty eyebrows.

squeeze_hold.narration: The loose roof will not stay up by itself. Someone holds it while a friend crawls through with the rope.

interaction.cue: Hold the roof while your friend crawls through with the rope.

onSuccess.narration: One by one, you come through, packs and all.

onFailure.narration: The roof sheds one more shower of chips. Nobody is hurt, just frostier.

onAssisted.narration: You wedge the rope hooks under the roof like two small props. They hold just long enough for everyone to come through.

seam_back.narration: You come out in a small round chamber. One wall is smooth and warm: the back of the sealed seam in the singing hall. Here the ticking is loud as a heartbeat. How will you test it?

seam_a.narration: You hum the hall note softly at the back of the seam, and wait.

seam_b.narration: You tap slow, slow, quick on the seam with a stone. Then everyone leaves a little silence for its answer.

seam_done.narration: The seam ticks back, quicker. Frost sparkles down the wall in a pattern, over and over, as if it wants you to say it back.

seam_echo.narration: The frost sparkles a pattern: tick, tock, tock, tick. The seam wants it said back. Everyone sees the sparkles a little differently.

interaction.cue: Watch the frost sparkle, then tap the same pattern.

onSuccess.narration: The seam hums, pleased, but stays shut. A line of light runs to a crack in the corner, narrow as a cat door. The ticking goes through it.

onFailure.narration: The seam sulks and stays shut. Then it slides a line of frost to a crack in the corner, narrow as a cat door. The ticking goes through it.

onAssisted.narration: You trace the pattern together. The seam stays shut, but a line of light runs to a narrow crack in the corner.

behind.narration: You slip through the corner crack into a narrow passage behind the singing hall. It smells of salt. Far off, the yetis in the hall hold their low note. Ahead, the ticking stops, and something shimmers.

passage.narration: The passage ends at a fold in the air. Beyond its shimmer, you smell salt wind and hear gulls. The light around the fold is called Riftlight. What will you try?

chime.narration: You strike the chime. Its note goes sour, with no echo. The way is not ready yet. In the quiet after, a lower note trembles under your feet.

variants.text: The chime answers with a clear note and an echo. The opening is still ready, and the way back is still there. Your first song was enough.

read.narration: Your starweaver studies the light. The others see only a shimmer. The opening hums back faintly. Nothing steps through, and nobody can name the place beyond.

listen.narration: You put an ear near the rock. Under the gull cries, a low note rises and falls. It matches the one you learned in the hall.

look.narration: Frost lines run toward the fold like the spokes of a wheel, and every line ticks. Beside it, someone long ago scratched a tally into the stone, one mark for each visit. There are not many marks.

beat.narration: The fold ticks, steady as a clock. The beat has an order, and everyone holds a clue. Which taps, in which order?

interaction.cue: Share your clues, then tap the beat in order.
clues: The beat starts with a slow tap.
Two slow taps come before anything else.
A quick tap ends the beat, with no rest.

beat_done.narration: Your taps and the ticking line up: slow, slow, quick. The fold brightens. A gull cries on the other side, very close. The fold is answering the hall note, the same note you sang to the seam.

beat_off.narration: The taps tumble into a clatter, and the fold dims. A puff of cold air ruffles your hair. You stop and listen instead: slow, slow, quick. It is the hall note, answered. The fold brightens again.

cairn.narration: The herder squeezes in from the hall's wide back door, with hay in her fur and the kid under her arm. She sniffs the salt wind and steps back. "My herd must never wander in there. Goats go through anything. How do we keep them out?"

cairn_a.narration: You and the herder stack blocks across the passage mouth, leaving a gap for people. She tests each block before she calls the kid back.

cairn_b.narration: You tie the herder's spare goat bells across the passage mouth. She checks their height against the kid, who tries to eat a bell.

cairn_smash.narration: A bigfoot lifts the biggest blocks. Smash, thump, thump! The others fit small stones into the gaps.

cairn_smash_check.narration: Your bigfoot sets the last broad block, and everyone marks a gap for travelers. The herder checks that no curious goat can squeeze through.

cairn_done.narration: The passage mouth is marked. Goats will stay out, and travelers will look before they step in. The herder pats the cairn like a friend's head. "There. It can be as strange as it likes on the other side."

herder_say.narration: "The ticking is the hall's note, answered from somewhere else," says the herder. "Maybe your song wakes it. Maybe it wakes whatever waits beyond. It is your road, not mine." She presses four coins from the hall's tin into your hand, and a small warm bead. "Keepers' fee. The bead was my grandmother's."

herder_share.narration: She eats it in two bites and looks embarrassed. "The hay is not the only thing running low." The kid gets the crust, and then eats her glove.

footing.narration: The herder scuffs the floor and frowns. Meltwater has left a slick skin of ice sloping toward the shimmer. "One wobble, and somebody slides in feet first." By the back door lie old planks and a little grit. The kid stares at a drip, fascinated.

footing_a.prompt: Chip small steps into the slick floor, deep enough to grip.

footing_b.prompt: Lay the planks on the safest line, and grit the thinnest ice.

footing_buy.narration: A young yeti trots up with a sack of grit and a sign that says GRIT. You spread it, and it bites into the ice. The kid eats a pinch and regrets it.

footing_done.narration: The floor grips your boots now. The herder stamps on it, then on the kid's tail by mistake, and everybody apologizes. Nobody will slide anywhere by accident.

footing_off.narration: A boot skids, and someone sits down hard. The thump makes the fold shiver. The herder hauls them up, laughing. The floor is rough, but it holds.

decide.narration: The hall seam answered your song. Here the fold itself ticks to the beat of that song. The herder waits by the cairn. Sing the hall note together and see what the fold does? Or leave it alone and go back to the hall?

hold.prompt: Everyone sings the low hall note and holds it to the end.

sing_wobble.narration: The note wobbles. Frost showers down someone's collar. Then the herder hums the low part from the cairn, deep and slow, and you find your note again. It is not tidy. It is enough.

sing.narration: You sing the low note. The ticking steadies. The fold widens, and salt wind brushes your cheeks. When you stop, it stays open. You answered it. You did not change its rules.

variants.text: You hum again. The opening stays just as wide. It does not need another note. It has stayed open since your first song.

test_open.narration: The chime answers with a clear note and an echo. The opening is ready, with a way back. Beyond, shallow water ripples around mud. Cross together, or go back to camp first.

variants.text: The opening stays wide after your song. Salt wind and gull cries keep coming. You could fetch the Listening Chime from camp before you trust it.

ready.narration: You stand together by the fold. The passage to the singing hall is behind you, and the herder's cairn guards its mouth. The air smells of a coast nobody can name yet.

leave.narration: The herder walks you back to the hall by the wide back door. The kid trots ahead. The cairn guards the passage mouth. The Cairnstep lead is still yours, and you can come back to sing the note later.

voiceGuide.tone: Warm, funny, curious, with real consequences. Describe actions and sensory details directly. Short dialogue. Never use "the kind of thing that", "the sort of thing that", or "it was X, the type of thing that makes you Y" comparisons. Let a character act instead of explaining how the reader should feel.
voiceGuide.vocabulary: Read aloud to an eight-year-old. Concrete words, short sentences, distinct voices.
